issue.title: Complete xprompt directive completion in ACE and external editors
issue.description: Give every supported xprompt directive, syntax form, keyword name, and useful keyword value one shared, responsive completion contract across the prompt input widget and the xprompt LSP.

issue.title: Canonical directive completion contract in sase-core
issue.description: directive-contract: define the complete directive and argument schema, grammar-aware cursor context, value-provider roles, and Python bindings in sase-core so frontends no longer maintain divergent hard-coded catalogs.

issue.title: Complete contextual directive support in the xprompt LSP
issue.description: external-editor-lsp: drive LSP names, snippets, keyword names, and contextual values from the shared contract, extending the existing cached editor catalog bridge for bead and identity targets without blocking editor requests.

issue.title: Complete responsive directive support in the ACE prompt widget
issue.description: prompt-widget: replace the prompt widget's private directive tables and token classifier with the shared contract, wire warm dynamic catalogs for bead, identity, model, and path values, and preserve the non-blocking completion path.

issue.title: Lock runtime, widget, and LSP parity with tests and documentation
issue.description: parity-verification: add exhaustive contract and interaction coverage for every directive and keyword, verify matching ACE/LSP behavior including failure degradation and UTF-16 edits, and document the complete completion matrix.

payload.entry:
DISCOVERED ISSUE: root cause for the missing .venv/bin/sase-xprompt-lsp reports on this epic (notes #2, #3, #4, #5, #6). Justfile's `rust-lsp-install` recipe builds with a bare `cargo build --release -p sase_xprompt_lsp` that does NOT pin CARGO_TARGET_DIR, so on any host whose ~/.cargo/config.toml sets `[build] target-dir` the binary lands there instead of under the checkout. The recipe then copies from the hard-coded `{{ sase_core_dir }}/target/release/sase-xprompt-lsp`, which never exists on such a host. Because that recipe body chains with ';' rather than '&&', the failed cp does not stop the recipe: it still prints '[rust-lsp-install] installed <dest>' and exits 0, so `just install` reports success while .venv/bin/sase-xprompt-lsp keeps whatever stale copy was there.

REPRODUCED 2026-08-28 in workspace sase_26 while landing epic sase-v2. `just install` printed:
  cp: cannot stat '<ws>/sase/repos/linked/sase-core/target/release/sase-xprompt-lsp': No such file or directory
  chmod: cannot access '<venv>/bin/sase-xprompt-lsp.tmp.2820361': No such file or directory
  mv: cannot stat '<venv>/bin/sase-xprompt-lsp.tmp.2820361': No such file or directory
  [rust-lsp-install] installed <venv>/bin/sase-xprompt-lsp
and still exited 0. Evidence: ~/.cargo/config.toml has `[build] target-dir = "/mnt/poseidon/cargo-target"`; `<ws>/sase/repos/linked/sase-core/target` does not exist; the freshly built binary is at /mnt/poseidon/cargo-target/release/sase-xprompt-lsp (mtime 2026-08-28 10:51, this run); .venv/bin/sase-xprompt-lsp was left at its stale 2026-08-26 08:27 copy. A fresh workspace with no prior copy is exactly the missing-binary case reported in notes #2-#6.

CONTRAST: the sibling `rust-dev-install` recipe does not have this bug — it exports CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$sase_core_abs/target/uv-tool-lsp" before building, so its cp source is correct by construction.

SUGGESTED FIX: pin CARGO_TARGET_DIR in `rust-lsp-install` the way `rust-dev-install` does (or resolve the real path with `cargo metadata --format-version 1`), and chain the cp/chmod/mv with '&&' so a failed install cannot report success. Not caused by epic sase-v2; routed here because this epic already owns the xprompt LSP install-path issue. No standalone task created.
